status: DRAFT estimate from teleop video, pending P0 physical measurements (D-205). Not a CameraProfile contract; do not load it on the robot.
rotate_note: Recorded frames are upright (floor at bottom); the 180 deg rotation from camera.yaml/line_follow.yaml was already applied before recording. Apply rotate_deg=180 to RAW sensor frames only; do not rotate the recorded mp4 again.
pitch_sign: positive = optical axis below horizontal (URDF rpy pitch convention)
roll_sign: camera x-axis (image right) tilted up by +roll; horizon row increases ~1.6 px per 100 px to the right
x_offset_note: prior from sim URDF, not measured

distortion.note: mild barrel, <=~2 px at the image corners; safe to ignore at 320x240

confidence_notes: fx: fitted to 54 crosswalk frames (216 corners, RMS 1.08 px) with the CAD bar proportions (26x121 mm, 40 mm pitch). Leave-one-group-out 280-284 px. Ring-circularity check on 93 frames gives 250-310 px, best-quality frames 280-285.
fy: the ground plane cannot separate it from pitch and height (first-order degeneracy). fx = fy (square pixels) is assumed, because libcamera crops to keep the aspect ratio.

horizon: 1707 per-frame lane vanishing points give a median row of 80.7, robust sd 2.6 px. The crosswalk poses give row 80.0. For a sim camera with a centred principal point, use pitch = atan((120 - 80.3) / fx).

cx, cy: not observable from this data (a free principal-point fit diverged). Centre is assumed. The mechanical pitch is then uncertain by about +-2 deg, but the horizon row, and so the ground mapping, is not.

height: scale-dependent. Crosswalk at 40 mm pitch gives 69.4 mm. The 155 mm wall gives 66 mm (near walls 66-69). The CAD lane c-c of 185 mm gives 63.7 mm. The physical mat's lane c-c to bar-pitch ratio is 5.1, against 4.62 in CAD, so the mat does not match the CAD exactly. One tape-measure reading of the lens height would resolve this.
sim URDF differs: 0.0602 m height (real is about 0.067 m), 66 deg hfov (real 59 deg), and the lane launches set cam_tilt_deg=25 (real is about 8 deg).
